_source: n8n OpenAPI spec v1.1.1 — GET /api/v1/projects + GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/users
_note: Projects organize workflows into teams. Combined with workflow shared[] and users, this maps the organizational structure behind automations.
_llm_can_infer: How the company organizes its automation work (by team? by function? personal?)
Which teams actively build automations (Sales, Support, etc.)
Team sizes per project — how many people collaborate on automation
Personal vs team projects — is automation centralized or distributed?
Project names often reveal business domains ('Sales Automation', 'Billing Ops')

_business_value.org_structure: Projects map to teams/departments. 'Sales Automation' + 'Customer Support' as separate projects = departmental automation ownership. This directly informs process clustering.
_business_value.process_hints: Project names are strong hints for business process grouping. If workflows are organized into 'Sales', 'Support', 'Finance' projects, the LLM should respect this organizational signal.
_business_value.collaboration_patterns: Multiple editors on a project = collaborative automation. Single editor = concentrated knowledge.
_business_value.automation_maturity: Many projects with clear names = mature automation practice. One 'Default' project with everything = early-stage, unorganized.
